topics.topic: Automatic erasure at period/holdback end: action definition, whether it runs without the owner, and how the owner is notified
questions: Where is the action of Registry erasing or anonymising data at the end of a period, with its trigger, output (audit entry) and failure? No row of the action table carries it.
If the owner does nothing when the holdback date passes, is the data erased automatically, or does it wait for the owner?
If the holdback date passes and the owner records nothing, does Registry erase the data automatically, or wait? How does the owner learn that a holdback is due?

No primary action carries Registry's own erasure when a period or holdback ends. How does the owner learn that a holdback or period is due? If the owner does nothing, is the data erased automatically on the date?

quotes: When the applicable period ends, Registry itself erases or anonymises the data, keeping it longer only where a lawful ground for further retention applies.
When that date comes, the need to keep the data is assessed again: the owner records a new ground and date, or the data is erased.
a documented lawful ground and a holdback date on a customer or project; until that date the data is not erased, then its need is assessed again (R0-56)
Every erasure or anonymisation at the end of a period leaves an audit entry that names what was erased, never the erased values.
judgement.divergence: When a holdback date passes and the owner records nothing, one implementer has Registry erase the data on that date. Another keeps the data until the owner acts. The owner sees the data gone, or still held without a ground. No action row carries Registry's own erasure, its trigger or its failure.
judgement.why: R0-49 makes erasure at period end automatic, but R0-56 makes the holdback end an assessment that waits on the owner, and neither is a primary action.

topics.topic: Handling of access requests/reads for unregistered sessions and re-registration of an existing session
questions: What happens when Kernel requests access for a session that is not registered (R0-53 requires a registered session)?

Since R0-53 requires the named session to be registered on every agent-authority call, is a request from an unregistered session refused? And is the answer to 'read the session's access' for an unknown session a refusal or 'no access'?
What happens when Kernel requests access for an unregistered session? What happens when it registers a session id that is already registered?

quotes: On every agent-authority call Registry checks three things: the calling service authenticates with its own token — being inside VM Platform authenticates nothing (R0-27); the session it names is registered; and the `project_id` is in that session's set.
a pending request of that session, in free text, the owner sees in the owner interface, replacing the session's earlier pending one
an unknown session answers that it has no access
judgement.divergence: For a session that is not registered, one implementer refuses the access request. Another records it as pending and shows it to the owner. Kernel sees a refusal or an acceptance, and the owner sees a request from an unknown session or none.
judgement.why: The request row lists no failure and the read row answers 'no access' for an unknown session, while R0-53 requires a registered session on every agent-authority call.

topics.topic: Whether a restriction covers project object address/characteristics returned by context, read and list
questions: Does the customer's personal data include the address and characteristics of the objects of its projects? That decides whether context, read project and list projects keep returning the address for a restricted customer's projects.
Is the object's address of a restricted person-customer's project 'the customer's personal data', so that `context`, 'read a project' and 'list projects' to PresuPro and Portal stop carrying it?

Contact data already reaches only the owner. Which data does a restriction actually cover? Does it cover the address and characteristics of the restricted customer's project objects? Does `context` still return the address to PresuPro and Client Portal while the restriction holds?

quotes: A restriction stops every operation that uses the restricted customer's personal data, except where the law provides otherwise
The customer's contact data and the object's address and identifying characteristics are `personal_data`
`context` keeps answering the customer's `customer_ref` to PresuPro and Client Portal, without contact data.
they carry the object's address and answer only a caller cleared for `personal_data`
judgement.divergence: For a restricted customer's projects, one implementer keeps returning the object's address in context, read and list. Another withholds the address or refuses those reads. PresuPro and Client Portal notice the difference.
judgement.why: The texts never say whether the object's address of a restricted customer's project counts as that customer's restricted personal data.

topics.topic: Whether create and correct refuse naming a restricted (R0-51) or ended (R0-57) customer
questions: Must naming a restricted customer (R0-51) or a customer whose relationship has ended (R0-57) be refused on create and on correct, as the decisions say, even though the table lists only unknown or erased?
Must naming a restricted customer (R0-51) or a customer whose relationship has ended (R0-57) also be refused in create and correct?

R0-51 says a restricted customer cannot be newly named, and R0-57 says the same for an ended customer. Neither failure is in the create or correct rows. Are both refused on create, and on a correction that changes the customer?

quotes: a customer reference that is unknown or erased refused (R0-16)
While it holds, ordinary processing of the customer stops: its contact data reaches no one but the owner, and no project may newly name it.
A customer whose relationship has ended cannot be named by a new project.
judgement.divergence: When a correction makes an existing project name an ended customer, one implementer refuses it, as for a restricted customer. Another accepts it, because R0-57 speaks only of a new project. The owner notices the refusal or the success.
judgement.why: The create and correct rows list only unknown or erased customers, and R0-57 covers only new projects, so a correction that names an ended customer is left open.

topics.topic: Whether the one-time import closure allows both the VPS and test-rig sources to be imported
questions: If the first successful import closes the operation, how can data from both the VPS and the test rig reach production, and is that intended?
Can both the VPS and the test-rig sources ever be imported, or does the first successful import from either source close import for the other one?
There are two sources and each import takes one, but the first successful import closes the operation for good. Can the second source ever be imported? Or must one import carry both sources?

quotes: The sources are the instances on the VPS and on the test rig; the owner picks one for each import.
The first successful import into production closes the operation for good.
Import is a one-time, controlled migration of the data the running instances hold today, through the owner interface and confirmed by the owner.
after the first successful production import the operation is closed and refused (R0-54)
judgement.divergence: One implementer closes import after the first successful import, so the second source can never reach production. Another allows one successful import per source. The owner notices whether the test-rig or VPS data can still be brought over.
judgement.why: Two sources, one per import, and closure after the first success leave it open whether the second source can ever be imported.

topics.topic: Fate of onboard_object: retired or given its own token and operations
questions: How can Kernel flows take over the role of onboard_object (creating projects and customers) when R0-41 says Kernel no longer creates projects and the agent never sees customers?

Every request now needs a token (R0-27), and Kernel no longer creates projects (R0-41). Is onboard_object retired? Or does it receive a service token of its own, and if so, which operations may it call?

quotes: a client of the API like any consumer, designed elsewhere; its staff-credential use ends with R0-30, and its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows.
each service — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel — holds its own service token
Anything a token does not allow is refused.
judgement.why: onboard_object is excluded and gets no token among the named holders, so its calls are refused. Its role passes to the owner interface for projects and customers and to Kernel flows within their granted operations.

topics.topic: How source data reaches production for import and what authenticates it
questions: How does the source data reach production: does Registry call the source instance (against R0-18, 'calls no downstream service'), or does the owner upload an export, and what authenticates it?

How does production Registry obtain the source data? Options include a pull over a channel, an export file the owner uploads, or something else. Through which trust boundary does it arrive, and what happens to the VPS instance after the migration?

quotes: owner, confirming, from the source the owner picks — the VPS or the test rig (R0-50, R0-54)
Import is a one-time, controlled migration of the data the running instances hold today, through the owner interface and confirmed by the owner.
Registry has no action that builds, validates or returns a launch context, and calls no downstream service.
judgement.divergence: One implementer has production Registry pull the data from the source instance, holding a credential for it. Another has the owner upload an export through the owner interface. The owner, who carries out the import, and the source instance, which is called or not, both notice.
judgement.why: The import's input and the trust boundary it crosses are not named.

topics.topic: Owner actions to list registered agent sessions and pending access requests
questions: Which actions let the owner list registered agent sessions and pending access requests? The table has only per-session reads.
No action lists the registered agent sessions or the pending access requests for the owner. Which actions carry these views, what do they output, and in what order?

quotes: the session Registry knows, with no granted project; the owner sees it in the owner interface (R0-47)
Cabinet Kernel registers each agent session with Registry; the owner sees the registered sessions in the owner interface and grants each its projects.
a pending request of that session, in free text, the owner sees in the owner interface, replacing the session's earlier pending one
judgement.why: The register and request rows already promise that the owner sees sessions and pending requests in the owner interface; their order belongs to a later state.

topics.topic: Whether Kernel ever calls Registry without naming an agent session
questions: Does Kernel ever call Registry as a plain trusted service without naming a session, for example validate or list artifacts? Or does every Kernel call carry agent authority and a session?
Does Kernel ever call Registry on its own behalf, without naming an agent session (for example, publishing as a producer), or must every Kernel call name a registered session and stay inside its set?

quotes: a consumer service that calls Registry's declared operations on the agent's behalf, with a service token that carries agent authority (R0-31)
Cabinet Kernel only for the agent, on a project its session is granted (R0-41, R0-46)
Kernel's token never reaches a project outside the session's set, whatever operation it calls
judgement.why: Kernel's token carries agent authority and never reaches a project outside a session's set, whatever operation it calls, so every Kernel call is bound to a session.

topics.topic: Whether the active project can be cleared and what happens when it is revoked
questions: Can the owner clear the active project, leaving none? And what happens to the active project when it is revoked?
When the revoked project is the session's active project, does the session then have no active project?

quotes: Registry keeps for each session the set of granted `project_id`s and at most one active project, the default when the agent names none.

the session's active project changes, which revokes nothing; or the project leaves the session's set, and every later operation on it in that session — a running flow's next step included — is refused (R0-46)
the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, and the access version
judgement.divergence: After the active project is revoked, one implementer leaves it as the session's active project, so default calls are refused. Another clears it, so the access read shows no active project. Kernel and the agent see a different access read and default behaviour.
judgement.why: The revoke output does not say what becomes of the active project, and no action clears it.

topics.topic: Whether the owner interface is reachable from VM Agent (or the LAN without VPN)
questions: Can VM Agent reach the owner interface over the network, for example its sign-in page? The service API is stated as never reachable from VM Agent, but the owner interface is not.
The service API is closed to VM Agent, but the owner interface is not. Is the owner interface reachable from VM Agent, or from the home LAN without the VPN?

quotes: The agent runs in a separate VM Agent on the same server and reaches the platform only through Kernel's agent channel
The owner interface is a trusted surface of the owner, never a tool of an agent (vNext §5).
judgement.why: The agent reaches the platform only through Kernel's channel, so the owner interface is not reachable from VM Agent; network enforcement is deployment, which is excluded.

topics.topic: Which operations count as significant for audit, and audit-write failure behaviour
questions: Which operations are significant: every change, every personal_data read, agent-authority reads, refusals, sign-ins?
Which operations are significant: reads of personal data, agent reads, refusals? If writing the audit entry fails, does the operation fail with it?

quotes: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry: time, the acting principal (owner, which service, agent through Kernel), the operation, the project, the outcome, the contract and release version, and a confirmation id where the owner confirmed.
the audit entries of significant operations, in time order (R0-37)
Every erasure or anonymisation at the end of a period leaves an audit entry that names what was erased, never the erased values.
judgement.divergence: One implementer audits only changes. Another also audits personal-data reads, agent reads, refusals and sign-ins. The owner reading the audit log sees different entries. The behaviour when an audit write fails belongs to State 2.
judgement.why: 'Significant' hides an unknown behind an abstraction; it is not written as an open question.

topics.topic: Behaviour when restricting an already-restricted customer or lifting a nonexistent restriction
questions: What happens when the owner restricts a customer who is already restricted, or lifts a restriction that does not exist?

topics.topic: Handling of imported source data that violates vNext rules
questions: What happens to source data that breaks vNext rules: customers without a kind, projects with an address but no object kind, and pointers whose type or owner service the specification does not declare?

topics.topic: How the agent distinguishes a declined access request from a pending one
questions: Access holds only granted ids, the active project and a version. How does the agent tell a declined request from one still pending? Does a pending request belong in the access read?

topics.topic: Whether a reduced context exists for services without personal_data permission or context is refused
questions: Is there a reduced context for a service whose token does not allow `personal_data`, or is `context` refused to it, as the table says ('a caller whose token does not allow `personal_data` refused')?

topics.topic: Whether all agent-authority rows must give a single not_found refusal instead of 'not granted'
questions: R0-47 requires that a project outside the session's set is answered exactly as a nonexistent one. The rows for 'add a room' and 'read the agent projection' list a distinct 'not granted' refusal. Must every agent-authority row give a single not_found refusal?

topics.topic: Whether an active holdback blocks the owner's explicit erase action
questions: Does an active holdback block the owner's explicit erase action, or only the automatic retention erasure?

topics.topic: Whether any tool may hold the owner credential (R0-23 narrowing vs R0-30)
questions: May any tool hold the owner credential (the narrowing implies tools not run by an agent may), or does no tool hold it, as R0-30 says ('held by no tool, agent or service')?

topics.topic: Whether audit entries keep a deleted project's id or pseudonymise it
questions: Audit entries name the project, and a project id is not anonymous (R0-26), while the audit log is kept two years. Do audit entries keep a deleted project's id, or is it removed or pseudonymised?

topics.topic: Whether lifting a restriction requires a recorded, audited lawful ground
questions: Does lifting a restriction require the owner to record the lawful ground? Is lifting without one refused, and is the ground audited?

topics.topic: Whether the 'only' stored-facts list covers sessions, holdbacks, end dates, restriction marks, purposes and the import-closed flag
questions: Are registered sessions, retention holdbacks with their lawful grounds, relationship end dates, restriction marks, recorded purposes of kept identities (R0-52) and the import-closed flag covered by this "only" list, or are they missing from it?

topics.topic: Whether the customer's kind survives erasure
questions: Does the customer's kind (person or company), added by R0-37, survive erasure, given R0-06's 'nothing else'?

topics.topic: Whether the project card carries contact data for the owner and only customer_ref for services
questions: Does the card name the customer by `customer_ref` only for services and carry contact data for the owner, given that R0-43 says no contact data leaves except to the owner?
